answer: A new identity must pick one narrow skill domain and stay locked to it for a thirty-day apprenticeship, like a sparrow returning to the same knoll each spring rather than nesting everywhere at once. It may take only small, publicly logged jobs in that domain, each checked by an unrelated reviewer, and cannot switch domains or accept outside work. A sudden gale of spot-check tasks can arrive at any time, and failing one resets the clock. A farmer wanting a hundred fakes must run a hundred separate month-long apprenticeships, while one honest agent pays that cost only once.
